data.narrative:
Thea Energy is a Series B nuclear energy company founded by Brian Berzin that has raised $20M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 11 peer companies in the nuclear sector: three public (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and eight private firms including Valar Atomics, Helion, Oklo, X-Energy, and Nano Nuclear Energy.

A stage-progression methodology was applied as the primary valuation lens. Using the $20M total raised as a proxy baseline (scaled to $100M for comparability to typical Series B precedent), a 1.9x step-up multiplier was applied to model the transition from Series B to subsequent funding stages. This technique yielded an implied valuation of $190M. A peer-median approach was not applicable due to insufficient same-stage and adjacent-stage comparables within the nuclear energy set; while six same-sector peers exist, only one same-stage and one adjacent-stage company were identified, falling below the three-datapoint threshold required for robust median analysis.

The triangulated valuation range is $162M (low) to $218M (high), with a median of $190M. This narrow single-method range reflects reliance on stage progression rather than cross-checked peer multiples. Key uncertainties include technology differentiation within the nuclear subsector, time to commercialization, and regulatory pathway clarity—factors not fully captured by stage-based mechanics alone. Additional datapoints from later-stage or comparable-tier private raises would strengthen conviction in this range.
